subject: Per-route sampling snapshot + graceful degradation plan for console
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Per-route sampling snapshot + graceful degradation plan for console

Hi team,

As we prep for the ACME onboarding next quarter, Product needs a concise per-route snapshot that surfaces token spend, p50/p95 latency, sampling rate, and a binary flag for whether a route has a fallback model. ACME is specifically asking for:

- A one-page snapshot we can hand to their SREs (CSV or console link)
- A recommended sampling policy for high-volume routes (we currently inadvertently drop long-tail traces)
- A graceful-degradation/fallback playbook we can publish in the console (priority: keep a short tail latency SLO while lowering cost)

I attached a suggested snapshot_template.csv and an excerpt of a sampled trace.

Questions:
1) Can runtime/observability export per-route p50/p95 + token-cost within the next 2 sprints?
2) What constraints would prevent us from marking a route as "has_fallback=true" automatically?
3) Can we include a link to a canary fallback route in the snapshot?

Markus / Marissa — please flag anything that will blow the schedule. Laura — this is a product ask for ACME; want to sync on priority.

Thanks,
Kimberly
--
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-route sampling snapshot + graceful degradation plan for console

Thanks for the ask, Kimberly — quick technical notes: 

On Thu, Apr 22, 2027 at 09:04 Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> As we prep for the ACME onboarding next quarter, Product needs a concise per-route snapshot that surfaces token spend, p50/p95 latency, sampling rate, and a binary flag for whether a route has a fallback model.

- We can export p50/p95 + token-cost per route, but the current metrics pipeline rolls up on a 1m window and we have a few sources of late-arriving telemetry (up to ~3m). If ACME needs second-level freshness we'll need a short roadmap item to reduce aggregation latency (OBS-4721).
- "has_fallback=true" can be derived if the route is configured with a fallback model ID in routing metadata. Problem: many legacy routes are dynamically generated and do not populate the metadata. We can add a heuristic that checks if there is an active fallback policy attached to the route's service, but it's a stopgap.
- Canary link: we can include the canary route URL if the route has an explicit canary tag in the routing table — otherwise we'd need a small UI change to let teams pin a canary target.

Estimate: export + CSV snapshot template -> 2 engineer-weeks (infra + metrics). Heuristic to infer fallback flag -> 3 engineer-days. Console link/canary pin -> 1 sprint UX + 2 dev-weeks.

I'll attach a sampled_trace_excerpt.log and a short checklist for the infra sprint.

- Markus
--
Markus Klein
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Per-route sampling snapshot + graceful degradation plan for console

Kimberly — thanks for pulling this together. A couple product-level clarifications so engineering can scope properly:

- Audience: this snapshot goes to (1) ACME SREs, (2) Redwood CS for renewal checks, (3) internal on-call. Let's make two output modes: "single-page summary" (high-level numbers) and "expanded CSV" (full per-route rows).
- For graceful degradation, priority is: preserve tail latency for customer-visible routes (non-batch RPCs) and allow cost-saving fallbacks for background/ingest routes. We should surface a binary "slo_sensitive" flag in the snapshot so SREs can filter.
- Timeline: ACME legal wants the snapshot and fallback plan in the onboarding pack by May 12. Can we target a minimal deliverable (single-page + heuristic fallback flag + canary link if present) by May 7?

Marissa — can you coordinate with Solutions to get ACME's list of critical routes (we shouldn't guess their SLO sensitivity).

Laura
--
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — summary and action items: 

1) Deliverable by May 7 (minimal): single-page CSV snapshot + heuristic fallback flag + include canary link when available.
2) Markus: start the export work and the fallback heuristic (2w + 3d work split). Please open OBS-4721 subtask for aggregation-latency improvements if you hit late-arrival >90s.
3) Marissa: please get ACME's critical route list and share in the Google Doc (link below) by EOD Apr 25.
4) Laura: I'll add the SRE/CS/Oncall use cases to the doc so the UX can decide summary vs expanded modes.
